#2 I guess they meant

x:X⊢a:A(x)x:X⊢(x,a):∑x′:XA(x′)\frac{x:X \vdash a:A(x)}{x:X \vdash (x,a) : \sum_{x':X}A(x')}x:X⊢(x,a):∑x′:X​A(x′)x:X⊢a:A(x)​

which I think is basically the right idea. But that’s not the usual rule either, since it doesn’t allow you to construct pairs in the empty context, unless you have a primitive substitution rule.

So the usual rule uses an arbitrary term of XXX:

t:Xa:A(t)(t,a):∑x:XA(x)\frac{t:X \qquad a:A(t)}{(t,a) : \sum_{x:X}A(x)}(t,a):∑x:X​A(x)t:Xa:A(t)​

This is the same as what you wrote, but with different notation.

content:
#4 Right, that’s why you’d need a substitution rule:

Γ⊢a : AΓ,x:A,Γ′⊢t : TΓ,Γ′[a/x]⊢t[a/x] : T[a/x]\frac{\Gamma \vdash a\,:\,A \qquad \Gamma,x:A,\Gamma' \vdash t\,:\,T}{\Gamma,\Gamma'[a/x] \vdash t[a/x]\,:\,T[a/x]}Γ,Γ′[a/x]⊢t[a/x]:T[a/x]Γ⊢a:AΓ,x:A,Γ′⊢t:T​

So combining this with the variables-only pairing rule (Γ′≔⋅\Gamma' \coloneqq \cdotΓ′:=⋅, a≔ta \coloneqq ta:=t, A≔XA \coloneqq XA:=X, t≔(x,a)t \coloneqq (x,a)t:=(x,a), T≔∑x′:XA(x′)T \coloneqq \sum_{x':X}A(x')T:=∑x′:X​A(x′)) we get:

Γ⊢t : XΓ,x:X⊢(x,a) : ∑x′:XA(x′)Γ⊢(t,a[t/x]) : ∑x′:XA(x′)\frac{\Gamma \vdash t\,:\,X \qquad \Gamma,x:X \vdash (x,a)\,:\,\sum_{x':X}A(x')}{\Gamma \vdash (t,a[t/x])\,:\,\sum_{x':X}A(x')}Γ⊢(t,a[t/x]):∑x′:X​A(x′)Γ⊢t:XΓ,x:X⊢(x,a):∑x′:X​A(x′)​

This is sufficiently general, since xxx need not be free in aaa. (And there’s actually no reason for xxx to be free in aaa when you just immediately substitute, since both ttt and aaa are provided together. What you really want is for xxx to be free in A(x)A(x)A(x), of course.)
